new.note: Thick-cut onion rings in crisp beer batter, stacked high with house sauce, argued over at the barbershop next door.
new.how: Thick onion rings dusted in flour, dipped in a cold lager batter and fried at 180C until crisp, stacked high with house sauce. Slice 3 large brown onions 1.5cm thick and separate the rings. Toss in 50g plain flour. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt with 250ml cold lager until smooth. Dip the rings and fry in batches for 3 minutes until golden, then drain and salt. Stir 125g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp sweet pickle relish, 1 tsp American mustard, 1/2 tsp paprika and 1 tsp white vinegar for the house sauce.

r2.make_ahead: Make the house sauce up to 2 days ahead and keep it chilled; batter and fry at the last minute

steps.text: Heat the oil to 180C in a deep pot.
Slice the onions 1.5cm thick, separate the rings and toss them in 50g of the flour.
Whisk the rest of the flour, the baking powder and salt with the cold lager until smooth.
Dip the rings in the batter and fry in batches until golden and crisp, 3 minutes a batch. Drain and salt.
Stir the mayonnaise, relish, mustard, paprika and vinegar into the house sauce.
Stack the rings high and serve with the sauce.

new.note: Crisp baked pastry pocket of hot cinnamon apple and brown sugar, McDowell's own version.
new.how: Shortcrust pockets filled with hot cinnamon apple and brown sugar, crimped and baked at 200C until crisp. Cook 3 diced Granny Smith apples with 30g butter, 40g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tbsp lemon juice for 8 minutes, then thicken with 1 tsp cornflour in a splash of water and cool. Cut 2 sheets shortcrust pastry into 4 rectangles each, fill one half, fold, crimp with a fork and cut two slits. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and bake at 200C for 22 minutes.

r2.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead; bake on the night so the pastry stays crisp

steps.text: Cook the apples with the butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice until just soft.
Stir in the cornflour mixed with a splash of water and cook until thick.
Heat the oven to 200C. Cut each pastry sheet into 4 rectangles, fill one half, fold over, crimp with a fork and cut two slits on top.
Brush with the egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and bake until crisp and golden.
